member_cost: 20% of the Medicare-approved amount after the $283 Part B deductible
requirements: Ordered by your doctor for use at home; use a supplier that accepts Medicare assignment
official_source_name: CMS - Your Medicare Benefits (official booklet, revised March 2026)
evidence_excerpt: Part B covers medically necessary DME if your doctor or other health care provider orders it for use in your home. … Medicare-covered DME includes, but isn't limited to: • Canes … • Walkers • Wheelchairs and scooters … After you meet the Part B deductible, you pay 20% of the Medicare-approved amount for DME (if your supplier accepts assignment). … In 2026, you pay a yearly $283 deductible for Part B-covered services and supplies.

official_source_name: CMS - Your Medicare Benefits (official booklet, revised March 2026)
evidence_excerpt: Medicare doesn't usually cover eyeglasses or contact lenses. However, Part B covers one pair of eyeglasses with standard frames (or one set of contact lenses) after each cataract surgery that implants an intraocular lens.

benefit_pathway: Part B preventive care - yearly Wellness visit

evidence_excerpt: If you've had Part B for longer than 12 months, you can get a yearly "Wellness" visit … You pay nothing if your provider accepts assignment. The Part B deductible doesn't apply.
